name: Skeld
loreTies: Source: Yggdrasil (world-tree, nine-world crossings, wyrd memory)
shortBackstory: Skeld commands the battlefield's geometry through world-root memory. He is the Yggdrasil-source: the one who reads the nine-world crossings and forces terrain to obey sacred thresholds.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Skeld was born from the world-root — the living architecture connecting the Nine Worlds. He is the controller: the one who sees the root system beneath every battlefield and bends terrain to Asgardian law. Ancient humans glimpsed him as Yggdrasil — but they saw only the tree, not the intelligence that moves its roots.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Among the Asgardian, Skeld is the terrain master. His world-root geometry creates threshold lines that enemies cannot cross without breaking a root-law.

chapters.title: Gate Wound
chapters.text: The Mythos Gate wounded Skeld by severing roots he did not know existed. The Hollow's erasure cut through the world-root like rot through a living tree — roots connecting to erased Realms simply went dark.

chapters.title: Campaign Role
chapters.text: In the Storm-Oath Covenant, Skeld controls the battlefield through world-root thresholds. His root-iron compass staff seals corrupted Gate lanes. But the Hollow creates dead roots — passages that lead nowhere.

chapters.title: Personal Conflict
chapters.text: Skeld's flaw is that he treats everything as geometry — including grief. When roots go dark, he reads it as a map error, not a loss. His conflict: is the controller who never grieves strong or simply numb?

relationshipHooks: Hrodda can test whether their courage is oath or vanity.
developmentStatus: Readable profile integrated into dashboard character pages.

human_echo: Frigg's silent fate-knowing became the Norns weaving destiny
